definition: In computational linguistics, a trigram tagger is a statistical method for automatically identifying words as being nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc.
details: based on second order Markov models that consider triples of consecutive words. It is trained on a text corpus as a method to predict the next word, taking the product of the probabilities of unigram, bigram and trigram. In speech recognition, algorithms utilizing trigram-tagger score better than those algorithms utilizing IIMM tagger but less well than Net tagger. The description of the trigram tagger is provided by Brants (2000).

explainer.lead: A trigram tagger is a statistical method for automatically identifying words as nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs and so on, based on second-order Markov models over triples of consecutive words. It matters as a corpus-trained approach to part-of-speech prediction.

tiers.eli5: It guesses each word's grammatical role by looking at the two words just before it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train it on a text corpus, taking the product of unigram, bigram and trigram probabilities; in speech recognition, trigram-tagger algorithms score better than IIMM taggers but less well than Net taggers.
tiers.paperLevel: The trigram tagger uses second-order Markov models considering triples of consecutive words, trained on a corpus to predict the next word by multiplying unigram, bigram and trigram probabilities; its description is provided by Brants (2000).

explainer.example: To tag a word, the tagger multiplies the relevant unigram, bigram and trigram probabilities and selects the tag.
